craft_notes: Same work voice as anu v1 (quatrain, dash breaths); new song, new sthāyin: adbhuta as the vision unfolds — bhakti in the mode of darśana, vyabhicāri camatkāra at the light-form person (C1 rasa block). Verse color: portrait, then vision, then silence. Firing rows: three parallel bahuvrīhi portrait-strokes -> parallel placement kept in one gathering line (row 3); compounds unpacked across the line-break (row 2); the close is the rupture AND the śānta-fall — Sanskrit ends not in statement but in question (vācyam kim atra adhikam, 'what more is to be said here?'). L3 states it ('past saying'); L4 restores the question: the verse silences itself by asking. Sanskrit-wins correction recorded here per ultimate-authority rule. FULL-LAYER AUDIT (all former layers re-read): L0 has no forks (all fork:none, single backfilled options) — it confirms rather than redirects: dual candrārkau (p003) + api too/even (p004) → 'themselves' carries both number and inclusion; pumāṃsam (p012) is accusative, the OBJECT of the vision → line 3 correctly an object-phrase, not subject; līnatām (p005, noun 'dissolvedness') + upagatau (p006, 'attained') → 'dissolved' collapse loses no aspect; atra (p022, 'here') absorbed into English 'there' — conscious thinning, vowel-arc cost of terminal 'here' judged higher than the deictic loss, recorded not hidden. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) L3 close 'so it stands, past saying.' → killed by Sanskrit interrogative kim (L0 p021) + NOTE 'the question is the period': stating what the verse asks drops a rank and kills the rupture. (b) Close with atra kept ('...to say here?') → killed by vowel arc: terminal 'here' lifts where 'say' settles; 'there' absorbs the deixis. (c) Portrait strokes split over two lines → killed by row 3: the three bahuvrīhis are one gathering breath, splitting flattens the parallel placement and breaks v1's quatrain-breath voice. (d) 'tip of the nose' → killed by row 2 density + singability; L3's hyphen-chain 'nose-tip' stands. (e) 'too' for api ('moon and sun too dissolved') → killed by economy: 'themselves' carries dual number + inclusion in one word. (f) Line-3 colon (L3's ':') → killed by voice continuity: v1 set dash-breaths, a colon would import a second caesura system. End-weight: the question is line-final and song-final — speech ends where the line ends. Vowel arc bright (Eyes, light) to dark (say). Read aloud: three long gathering lines, one short closing question — the breath stops where speech stops.

lines: Eyes half-open, mind steady, gaze set on the nose-tip —
moon and sun themselves dissolved within the triple throb —
a form of light, free of all outside, the one supreme Person —
reality attains that state, the highest Real. What more is there to say?
notes: Close restores Sanskrit interrogative (vācyam kim atra adhikam) against L3 declarative; trispandabhāva kept transliterated per L3 note (breath-vs-consciousness open)
l4.sanskrit_cite: ardhoddhāṭitalocanaḥ sthiramanā nāsāgradattekṣaṇaḥ candrārkāvapi līnatāmupagatau trispandabhāvāntare | jyotīrūpamaśeṣabāhyarahitaṃ caikaṃ pumāṃsaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tatpadameti vastu paramam vācyaṃ kimatrādhikam

What more is there to say here?
